chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: Arrangers for Hines and for Lunceford
summary: Mundy, Cecil Irwin and others wrote for Hines, and Lunceford's band had many unsung arrangers such as Billy Moore, Eddie Durham and Don Redman.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Who all were arranging for Earl's band for the shows? (Inaudible)

Oh, several people. Let me see. Some guys not even in the band. Let me see. Jimmy Munday and Cecil Irwin did most of the arranging. The one got killed, the tenor man I told you (Inaudible) -- until he got killed. They did most of the writing, but he had three or four guys -- Joe Massick, he did writing. You probably never knew him. He's from the downtown Loop in Chicago. But he had several people -- writers that
you never heard much about that did a lot of writing too for the band. Zilner Randolph would do somethings.

Zilner used to write for Louis years ago, you know. And he'd do a few things for Earl. It's just like Lunceford's band. Lunceford had quite a few -- Lunceford had quite a few arrangers at -- in that band that -- that wrote for that band and never played with him, you know. People -- one of the best arrangers we had was William -- Billy Moore -- William Moore, Junior. He went to Europe years ago. But he wrote things like "What's your story, Morning Glory" and those things for Lunceford's band.

Nobody -- if you mention Billy Moore -- William Moore, nobody know who it was. But we knew. And then he had another guy, Roger Segur. He had another guy Bud Estees. Don Redman used to write for Lunceford. See, all these people that you never knew. You'd say oh, that's the Lunceford sound. But that's not so. That was a lot of different arrangers were writing for that band. Anybody who made a good arrangement.
Eddie Durham did a lot of good arrangements for Lunceford's band. But you don't hear those names associated with Lunceford. All you hear is Sy Oliver and Eddie Wilcox, you know.
Willie Smith did a few little things.

But you never hear these other guys name who did some very fine things. Don Redman wrote a song and made arrangement on it for Lunceford. A good song and Dan Grissom sang it. "I'm losing my mind because of you".
